page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 118 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is average at 2215.58, while multi-core performance is poor at 2263.98, reflecting the limitations of its single physical core. Memory performance is mixed; the PassMark memory score is average at 1927.71, but memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only speeds of 168.1 GB/sec for small blocks and 22.92 GB/sec for large blocks, alongside a poor large-block write speed of 12.15 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and integer operations.

This instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight web serving. However, its low multi-core performance and weak database operation benchmarks suggest it is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compute tasks or high-throughput transactional databases.
